newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Analysts mixed on UBS first half results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts mixed on UBS first half results.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS ) posted a good overall result on Tuesday for the first half of 1997 but disappointed markets with flat trading income and higher than expected costs, analysts said.
Analysts polled by Reuters gave mixed reactions to six-month results from Switzerland's biggest bank, where group net surged 67 percent to a record 1,865 million Swiss francs ($1.2 billion).
The result was at the high end of forecasts of between nearly 50 percent and 70 percent. But operating profit rose 8.5 percent to 2,848 million, lower than expectations of 10 to 15 percent.
Analysts universally singled out trading income as a problem.

UBS said trading income rose only one percent to 1,310 million Swiss francs despite booming world financial markets, depressed by a 52 percent drop in revenue from equity trading caused by derivitives.
"Overall it is a good result. The biggest surprise is the flat trading income, given the environment," said Claudia von Tuerk at Geneva private bank Pictet & Cie.
"These things do happen in trading, but it's still a bit disappointing," she said.
On the plus side, von Tuerk said commission and fee income was very strong at a growth rate of 35 percent and interest income was also relatively strong at six percent higher.
Madeleine Hofmann from Credit Suisse First Boston said she was not happy at the overall results.
"Cash flow was disappointing, because trading income stagnated while costs rose 20 percent," she said.

UBS said operating expenses rose 20 percent, including an 18-percent rise in personnel costs due to appreciation of the pound and dollar against the Swiss franc and to bonuses for successful traders and asset managers.
"I am somewhat disappointed," said Christoph Bieri from Zurich Kantonalbank.
"Except for the fact that the bottom line net profit figure is higher, the middle figures are below what I was expecting," Bieri said.
Bieri had forecast operating profit to rise 13.5 percent.
Analysts were unsure what exactly caused the fall in equities trading income and hoped for more deatils from a telephone conference with UBS set for 4:00 p.m. (1400 GMT).
They speculated that UBS had gone short in expectation of falling stock markets and then been forced to buy shares at rising prices.
"But that is what risk management is supposed to do, keep things like this under control," Bieri said.

Pictet's von Tuerk said the results shed a positive light on upcoming half-year statement from UBS's two big rivals, Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) and Credit Suisse Group , due on August 13 and August 27 respectively.
"SBC and Credit Suisse should have good trading income, they are quite strong in that side of the business," she said.
"On commission income, if UBS is anything to go by, then the other two will probably have very good revenue growth.
However, she said Credit Suisse could have higher costs than UBS because of hiring people to expand its investment banking side.
SBC had costs under cotnrol but might need to put more aside in provisions for bad loans than UBS or Credit Suisse, she said.
Pictet was maintaining its ratings of UBS as a "buy" and the other two banks as "holds", von Tuerk said.
CSFB's Hofmann and Bieri at Zurich Kantonalbank also said they saw no reason in the first-half report to change UBS, which they have as a "hold".
Forecasts for Swiss Bank Corp first-half net profit range between 50 and 68 percent while Credit Suisse Group covers a wide field between 40 percent and 90 percent.
($ = 1.525 Swiss Francs)
